resources.string: Choose a PIN to protect the app. You\'ll enter this each time you open the recorder.\n\nMust be 4+ digits and not a common pattern.
Choose a secret digit sequence to unlock the app. Type these digits on the calculator then press = to enter.\n\nMust be 4+ digits and not a common pattern.
Too easy to guess — choose a less obvious code

This stops recording, destroys this app's encryption keys and attempts to delete local recordings and proof files.

Copies in selected folders (SAF), cloud storage and other backups are not deleted. Complete erasure of flash storage cannot be guaranteed.

This cannot be undone.
Uninstall this app? Uninstalling does not delete external copies or guarantee removal of all traces.
\n\nWithout these steps the system may kill recording within minutes of the screen turning off.
No audio or video captured — check permissions
Recording video only — check mic permission/availability
SAF upload failed — check folder permissions

Xiaomi/MIUI detected. For reliable recording:
1. Go to Settings → Apps → Manage apps → %1$s 2. Enable \"Autostart\" 3. Under \"Battery saver\", choose \"No restrictions\" 4. Lock the app in Recent Apps (swipe down on the card)

Samsung detected. For reliable recording:
1. Go to Settings → Battery → Background usage limits 2. Add %1$s to \"Never sleeping apps\" 3. Go to Settings → Apps → %1$s → Battery → Unrestricted

Huawei/EMUI detected. For reliable recording:
1. Go to Settings → Battery → App launch 2. Find %1$s and set to \"Manage manually\" 3. Enable Auto-launch, Secondary launch, and Run in background

OPPO/Realme/OnePlus detected. For reliable recording:
1. Go to Settings → Battery → App battery management 2. Set %1$s to \"Allow background activity\" 3. Lock the app in Recent Apps (swipe down on the card)
Camera permission required. Go back and start a recording first.
Tests %1$ds of video with your saved recording settings. A resolution passes only after its video can be decoded and a preview frame is saved.

The reference is the largest full-aspect video size at the highest supported normal rate, up to 30 FPS. Photo megapixels do not determine video resolution. Reject any smaller mode that loses a scene edge.
Send recordings to your chosen server. Upload encryption is selected separately in Settings.
Use a revocable app password, never your login password. This build requires HTTPS.
How do I get an app password?
Use an independently obtained SHA-256 public-key pin to restrict accepted HTTPS certificates.
Optional: independently verified SHA-256 SPKI fingerprint
Enter the server URL, username, and app password first.
✓ Connected. The server accepted your app password.
✗ Could not connect. Check the URL and app password (and that Tor is running if this is an .onion address).

sha256/%1$s
Verify this matches your server out-of-band (e.g. on the server console) before you trust it, then Save.
Could not retrieve the TLS certificate. Check the HTTPS address and network settings.
Server URL, username, and app password are required

1. Log in to Nextcloud in a browser. 2. Click your avatar → Settings → Security. 3. Under \"Devices & sessions\", type an innocuous name (e.g. \"Backups\"). 4. Click \"Create new app password\". 5. Copy the generated password (shown only once) and paste it above.
An app password is separate from your login password and can be revoked individually — good practice if a device is ever lost or seized.
Record audio and video with integrity proofs for later checks. Proofs do not establish scene truth, exact capture time, or completeness by themselves.
Hashes and signatures help check downloaded recordings for changes. A trusted checkpoint is needed to assess completeness.
Recordings are encrypted on the device and can be routed through Tor.
Uploads go to storage you control — a folder or your own Nextcloud.
During recording the app processes short segments. Choose a backup folder and connection before sending files.
Video and audio are captured in short segments.
Segments are linked by hashes. The app requests timestamp proofs when network settings allow.
Finished segments are encrypted for local storage. Temporary unencrypted files exist during processing.
Recordings are sent according to your chosen destination, upload encryption and network settings.
The verification tool checks integrity and available timestamp proofs. It cannot by itself establish the truth of a scene, exact capture time or completeness.
You\'ll enter this each time you open the app. Choose 4+ digits that aren\'t an obvious pattern.
You can add a duress code later in Settings. It starts key destruction and local cleanup; cloud and SAF copies remain.
PIN must be at least 4 digits
That PIN is too easy to guess
Video needs camera access. Microphone access is needed only when recording audio. Notifications let the app show a persistent recording indicator.
You\'re all set. You can change these anytime in system settings.
This controls what metadata goes into your recordings. You can change it later.
Reduces device, network and language metadata and disables GPS. Footage and remaining metadata may still identify you. An unsigned hash chain is recomputable.
Keeps additional device and environment metadata and signs proof records. This may identify the device and, if GPS is enabled, the location. It does not guarantee acceptance as legal evidence.
Choose where to save copies. Folder selection is recommended; Nextcloud is another option.
Upload to your chosen Nextcloud server over HTTPS. Tap to review the connection.
Connect a Nextcloud server with guided setup and an HTTPS connection test.

In the file picker, tap the menu at the top left (☰). If Google Drive, Dropbox or another cloud app is installed and signed in, choose it from the side menu, then select a folder. Only services that support folder access appear here. You can also choose a folder on this phone.

Copies are uploaded as ordinary, playable files by default. Recipient encryption and recording mode are in Settings → Advanced settings. You can choose a folder later; pending files use space on this phone.
By default, uploads use any available Wi-Fi or mobile connection. Choose VPN or Tor below if you need that requirement.
Direct cloud requests use the Orbot proxy and wait if it is unavailable. This does not route browser authorization or another app\'s SAF cloud sync. Tor is slower and requires Orbot.
VPN · requires one to be running
Uploads wait unless Android reports an active VPN. You configure the VPN yourself; check that it covers this app. VPN detection alone does not verify its route or trustworthiness.
Uploads go over whatever connection you have. Your network operator sees when you upload and to where; your storage provider sees your real IP address.
Pending files remain in the encrypted local queue while waiting for the required connection. Available storage is limited: check the queue and test delivery before use.
Not installed. Orbot is a free app from the Guardian Project that provides the Tor connection this setting uses.
Installed. Open it and tap Start, then come back — this screen re-checks automatically.
Uploads will go out over your normal connection, with your real IP visible.
Orbot proxy reachable. The Tor network requirement is satisfied; delivery still needs a working destination.
Uploads are blocked: Tor is selected, but Orbot isn\'t running yet.
VPN detected. The VPN network requirement is satisfied; delivery still needs a working destination.
Uploads are blocked: no VPN detected, and Tor is off.
Before first use, make a test recording and check that you can download and open the copy on another device.
Consider a duress code in Settings. Entering it attempts local cleanup and key destruction. It does not remove cloud or SAF copies or guarantee complete erasure.
Fewer frames · same native resolution · 15 fps
Higher quality · up to 1080p · target 30 fps
Maximum resolution · 30 fps · higher battery and storage use
Custom native frame rate and bitrate
Choose folder · phone or supported cloud service
Dropbox links uploads to your account. Provider access and legal disclosure depend on its service terms and applicable law. Choose recipient encryption if the provider must not read the content.

Google Drive links uploads and metadata to your account. Provider access and legal disclosure depend on its service terms and applicable law. Choose recipient encryption if the provider must not read the content.
WebDAV: assess who controls the server and where it is hosted. HTTPS protects transport; recipient encryption separately protects file contents from the server.
Nextcloud: choose a server you trust. Use HTTPS and a revocable app password; choose upload encryption separately.
App key from Dropbox App Console
Connecting Dropbox fills in the tokens and enables renewal. An access token alone is temporary.
Optional: independently verified SHA-256 SPKI fingerprint
Already set — type a new code to change

Entering this code on the lock screen or calculator starts key destruction and local cleanup. External copies remain, and complete erasure is not guaranteed. Use a different code from your unlock PIN.
Unlock code must be 4+ digits and not a common pattern
Duress code must differ from unlock code
Duress code is too easy to guess

Adds a second launcher icon that looks like a calculator; your PIN followed by = unlocks the recorder.\n\nWARNING: calculator-disguise apps are a known pattern that forensic tools and border agents can identify. Being caught with a deceptive app may be more incriminating than a visible recorder with a lock screen. Only enable if disguise fits your threat model.
Evidence · full device & environment metadata for court use
Anonymous · strips device fingerprint, network, locale

Evidence mode keeps additional device and environment metadata and signs proof records. Anonymous mode reduces identifying metadata and disables GPS, but footage and remaining metadata can still identify you. Hashes help check consistency; an unsigned chain can be recomputed. Completeness needs a trusted checkpoint.
Include GPS coordinates in proof metadata
WARNING: GPS reveals your physical location. Only enable if you want location evidence in your proof files. Disable for anonymity.
GPS is disabled in Anonymous mode
Require secure network (VPN or Tor) for uploads
Blocks external uploads until the selected network condition is met. When Tor is enabled its proxy must be reachable; otherwise Android must report an active VPN. Test your VPN routing separately.
Route app traffic through Tor (requires Orbot)
Direct cloud and timestamp requests use Orbot\'s SOCKS5 proxy. Browser authorization and other apps\' SAF sync use their own network settings. This setting alone does not route those apps.

Tor routing requires Orbot (Guardian Project).

1. Install Orbot
2. Open it and tap Start
3. Come back and enable Tor here

If you use a VPN instead, you don't need Orbot — just enable 'Require secure network' above.
Orbot is installed but the proxy is not running. Open Orbot and tap Start.
sha256/%1$s\n\nVerify this matches your server out-of-band (e.g. on the server console) before trusting it, then Save.
Could not retrieve the TLS certificate. Check the HTTPS address and network settings.

Unencrypted uploads let the storage provider and account holders read footage and proof metadata. HTTPS/Tor transport and local queue encryption remain independent. Encrypted uploads require the recipient’s private key to open.
Recipient RSA public key (PEM). Keep the private key off this phone.

Queued files keep their saved encryption choice and destination. Files without a saved choice still wait for configuration. Tor settings here do not route the traffic of separate folder-provider apps.
Enter a valid RSA public key (2048–8192 bits), or choose unencrypted uploads.
Cannot retain access to this folder. Choose a writable folder.
Enter the Dropbox app key first.
Open Dropbox, approve access, then paste the code here. Your browser uses its own network settings; app Tor routing does not cover it.
Connected. Save Settings to use this account.
Connection failed. Check the network settings and start authorization again; the code may have expired.
Unencrypted uploads: provider can read recordings
Uploads paused: choose upload encryption in Settings
Network requirement met; delivery still depends on the destination
Uploads blocked: start a VPN or enable Tor
Keys removed; local cleanup attempted. Restart resumes cleanup. Remote copies are unchanged.
Wipe incomplete. Close and restart the app to retry local cleanup.
Could not configure the camera for recording.
Could not start recording. Check app permissions and try again.
Could not finish processing the segment. Check available storage.
Could not create the MP4 recording. This segment may not have been saved.

1. Enter the Dropbox app key supplied with your build, then choose Connect Dropbox in browser.
2. Open authorization, sign in on www.dropbox.com and approve access. Copy the code, return here and choose Connect.
3. Save Settings, choose an upload folder and select Upload encryption. Save again.
4. Download a harmless test recording and its proof files on another device. Check playback or decryption and verification before use.

The connection uses PKCE and a refresh token. Never enter an app secret on the phone. If authorization expires, start it again.

The browser uses its own network settings. This app's Tor setting covers direct Dropbox requests, not browser sign-in.

For maintainers: register one scoped App Folder app in the Dropbox App Console with account_info.read, files.content.write, files.metadata.read and files.metadata.write. Distribute its public app key. A public release may require Dropbox production approval.

Unencrypted uploads are readable by the provider and anyone with account access. Recipient-encrypted .jwe files require the recipient's private key and cannot be previewed as videos in Dropbox. Pending files keep their saved destination and encryption choice.

Google Drive setup uses OAuth tokens entered manually. There is no guided browser sign-in for Drive in this screen. Prefer the guided Dropbox or Nextcloud setup if you need simpler configuration.

For a short test:
1. Open https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground
2. Select Drive API v3 and the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file
3. Choose Authorize APIs and approve access.
4. Choose Exchange authorization code for tokens.
5. Copy Access token into the access-token field here.
6. Choose a destination folder, select upload encryption, and save.

Access tokens expire. Do not rely on a manually pasted token for unattended recording. The provider has refresh-token support in code, but this screen does not offer a complete guided Google client-credential setup.

Download a test recording and proof files on another device and check them. Browser sign-in uses the browser's own network settings. Never share tokens in screenshots or support reports.

Enter the full HTTPS WebDAV endpoint, username and password. For Nextcloud, prefer the dedicated Nextcloud option and use an app password rather than your login password.

Nextcloud endpoint:
https://YOUR_SERVER/remote.php/dav/files/YOUR_USERNAME/
For a server installed in a subfolder, include that subfolder before /remote.php.

For other WebDAV servers, copy the endpoint provided by the administrator. It is not a public share link. Choose a writable destination folder, select upload encryption and save.

Test the connection, then send a harmless recording and download it with its proof files on another device. A successful connection test does not prove that file creation, upload and readback work.

If authentication fails, check the username, app password and folder permissions. If TLS fails, check the certificate and HTTPS address; do not bypass certificate validation. Browser and other apps' traffic do not inherit this app's Tor setting.

1. Sign in to Nextcloud in a browser. Open account settings → Security → Devices & sessions and create an app password. Copy it; do not use your main login password.
2. In guided setup, enter the HTTPS server base URL, for example https://cloud.example.com or https://cloud.example.com/nextcloud. Do not enter a public share link or full WebDAV path.
3. Enter your actual username, app password and destination folder. Create nested folders on the server first.
4. Test the connection and save. Then select Upload encryption in Settings and save.
5. Send a harmless recording, download the footage and companion proof files on another device, and test playback/decryption and verification.

The dedicated integration sends large files in chunks and checks uploaded content by downloading it again. This uses extra bandwidth and does not guarantee future retention. Recovery after every type of interruption has not been verified on all servers.

HTTPS is required, including for .onion addresses. If Tor is enabled, start Orbot. The browser uses its own network settings.

An optional SHA-256 SPKI fingerprint restricts accepted server certificates. Verify it independently, for example through the server console. Fetching a fingerprint alone does not authenticate the server.

A connection test does not prove write access. Check quota, folder permissions and server/proxy limits if uploads fail. Pending files keep their saved destination; finish the queue before changing accounts. App-password revocation does not erase files already uploaded.
Changes immediately. Save any other settings before switching languages.
Not uploading: choose encrypted or unencrypted uploads.
Not uploading: the recipient public key is missing or invalid.
Not uploading: configure a destination and its login details.
Not uploading: folder access is missing. Select the folder again.
Not uploading: this external SAF app cannot use the recorder’s Tor/VPN policy. Use direct Nextcloud/Dropbox or review network settings.
Waiting for a network connection. Files remain queued on this phone.
Not uploading: start Orbot/Tor. Files remain queued.
Not uploading: a VPN is required but none is detected.
Some queued files belong to the previous destination. Restore its account/folder to send them.
Upload failed. Files remain queued for retry; check the connection, account, quota and destination.
Choose before continuing. Ordinary MP4 uploads work without a recipient key. Recipient encryption requires a key. Without an explicit choice, nothing is uploaded.
You can record locally now, but there is no confirmed backup outside this phone. Queued files will be retried once the upload requirements are met.
Recording — video and audio are arriving
Video missing — only audio is arriving
Audio missing — only video is arriving
Recording stalled — no recent camera/microphone data
Segments saved to the local queue this session: %1$d
Sending/checking a file — delivery is not yet confirmed
Files queued — waiting for an upload attempt
Queue empty. Files saved to the selected folder; cloud synchronization is not confirmed.
Queue empty. The server accepted the sent files.
Waiting for the first completed segment to upload
No files queued. No delivery confirmed since the app process started.
Waiting: %1$d files (%2$.1f MB) · Confirmed since app restart: %3$d files
Cannot confirm upload status. Do not assume files have arrived.
Tap to check upload status and pending files.
A preview from each passing resolution is stored encrypted inside the app. Test clips are deleted; previews are never uploaded or added to your gallery. Testing stops when you leave this screen.
Saved frame is from an earlier test. Run the test again before choosing this resolution.
Could not save the default resolution. Try again.

This is a frame from native camera-to-encoder capture. Only this preview is resized for the screen. The video itself is not resized or padded by the app. Compare all four scene edges against the reference while keeping the phone still.
The default uses the largest full-aspect native video size at the normal frame rate, with no added resizing. Compare test frames before choosing a smaller size.

Video goes directly from the camera to the encoder. No app scaling, padding, frame dropping or interpolation. Presets change camera FPS and automatic video bitrate, never audio. The largest compatible native full-aspect mode is the reference. A smaller native mode requires a frame comparison in calibration. Changes to FPS or camera settings invalidate that comparison and restore the reference resolution. Battery savings depend on the phone and must be measured.

CameraX uses the same continuous encoder and segment writer. Compatibility testing is still pending. Save, then run camera calibration before a test recording. Do not rely on this experimental option for critical evidence yet. If it fails, stop recording and select Camera2; switching is never silent.
The camera system could not maintain capture. Stop, check the saved segments, and try Camera2 or recalibrate. Video may be missing.
No completed recording measurements yet. Record and stop normally to save a report.
Connected to power at a measurement endpoint

The latest completed session is kept for each camera system and profile, encrypted on this phone. FPS is the session average of encoded video timestamps. Gaps are diagnostic clues, not proof of missing frames. Traffic is all app traffic during the session, including retries and verification; later uploads and traffic from a separate SAF provider are excluded. It is not a cloud-delivery receipt. Battery percentages are coarse and temperatures are battery readings. Compare repeated 10–15 minute unplugged sessions with the same lighting, screen state, network and upload settings. No battery-life forecast is made.

%1$s — %2$s
Duration: %3$s s · %4$d × %5$d
FPS: target %6$d / measured %7$s
Largest frame gap: %8$s ms · non-increasing timestamps: %9$d
Encoded media: %10$s MB
App traffic: sent %11$s MB / received %12$s MB
Battery: %13$s → %14$s %%
Battery temperature: %15$s → %16$s °C
%17$s
The native full-view mode is unavailable or failed. Check camera calibration. The app will not resize or switch to a cropped fallback.

First test the reference and compare it with the normal 1× view in the Camera app. Keep the phone still when testing smaller sizes. To use one, compare both saved frames and confirm all four scene edges are preserved. Changing the frame rate or camera settings requires a new comparison.
Minimum frame rate · same native resolution · 10 fps
This camera does not advertise a native %1$d fps mode with a minimum of 10 fps. Select an available rate in Settings. No faster capture with frame dropping will be substituted.
The camera is delivering fewer than 10 fps. Check lighting, heat and camera settings; the requested minimum is not being sustained.
Advertised native FPS choices: %1$s. Unavailable presets are disabled. Exposure or heat can still lower the actual rate; check measured FPS. Savings are not guaranteed.
Test the full-resolution reference and this mode with the current settings before comparing.
Does the whole scene remain visible?

Confirm only if the phone stayed still and the same top, bottom, left and right scene edges are visible in both frames. If unsure or any edge is missing, cancel and keep the full-resolution reference. This is your visual confirmation, not an automatic optical verification.
Same full view — use this mode
Only native frame rates supported at this resolution are shown (minimum 10 FPS). Fewer frames can reduce battery and data use; the view and audio stay the same. Savings vary by phone.
Video uses H.264. Changing the frame rate leaves audio settings unchanged.
Videos go directly into the chosen folder. Proofs, timestamps and telemetry go into its Evidence subfolder, created automatically. Keep both when copying or sharing evidence.

Lower bitrate means smaller uploads, but less detail, especially in motion. It keeps the same camera view, resolution, frame rate and audio. Battery savings are not guaranteed. Changes apply to your next recording.
Automatic bitrate follows resolution, frame rate and quality. A fixed value is a target, not an exact file-size limit; the phone must support it.
About %1$.1f MB/min of video at the target rate, plus audio and metadata. Actual size varies with the scene and encoder.
Enter a whole number from 200 to 50000 kbps.
This encoder cannot use %1$d kbps. Its supported range is %2$d–%3$d kbps. Choose another bitrate in Settings.
This encoder does not support target bitrate control. Recording could not start.
Video bitrate: target %1$s kbps; measured %2$s kbps (audio excluded).
Allow camera access to see the live view.
Camera view unavailable. Check recording status below.
Choose before starting. When off, the microphone is not used and videos have no audio track.
Enable video or audio before recording.
Could not change the flash. Try again.
Recording was interrupted. Recovering saved footage… Please wait.
Some footage still needs recovery. Tap Retry upload. If this continues, save the available recordings and seek technical help; do not uninstall the app.
Recording was interrupted. Saved footage has been recovered where possible. The final moments may be missing. Tap Record to start again.
Not enough free space to record safely. Recording has stopped or cannot start. Free space in other apps; saved footage here is kept.
Recording stopped because the phone could not save video quickly enough. Saved footage is kept. Let the phone cool down, then try again.
Recording stopped because footage could not be saved safely. Saved footage is kept. Free some space and try again; do not uninstall the app.

Sound recording fell behind. Recording has stopped to prevent unsynchronized clips. Saved footage is retained. Before relying on another recording, make a test clip and check that sound and picture stay synchronized.
Automatically reduce video size when uploads fall behind (default minimum 1.5 Mb/s)
Automatic bitrate is unavailable on this phone; recording continues at the configured rate.
Recording has started. You can lock the phone with its side button.
Allow background operation so battery saving is less likely to stop recording. In the phone settings, allow the request or choose Unrestricted / No restrictions for this app.
Android battery optimization is disabled for this app. Manufacturer restrictions can still apply.
Android battery optimization is still enabled for this app.
Open the phone settings, find this app, then review its battery and background options.
Return here after changing the settings. You can continue without changing them, but test recording with the screen locked before relying on it. These options are also available in Settings.
